summary: Two automated checks failed: a level 2 head-on deadlock that stops the level from ending, and a front impact on a sedan that pays 374 when the spec says 228. I confirmed the deadlock from the source: a locked car stays displaced in the oncoming lane, and a stalled lower-serial car that never yields blocks the car it is facing. The damage formula in testImpact matches the spec, so the 374 figure needs reproducing. Solid cars, barriers, push-out and drawing look broadly in place.

defects.problem: Level 2 head-on deadlock. A car swerves into the oncoming lane band, because latFree only rejects an oncoming band when the move reduces lateral distance or the sweep rectangle already touches a car. The lock never releases, so the car stays there. When an oncoming car arrives, the lower-serial car does not yield, and axisMove sets its speed to the blocker's speed (0), so both stop permanently. The level never ends. Seen in seed 7: SDN-01 at y=292 eastbound against SPT-11 and VAN-07 westbound at y=284.

The damage check fails: a sedan front impact paid 374 instead of 228 in the check scenario. The closing speed in testImpact (c.vx/vy minus d.vx/vy) is evidently not 138. Likely causes are a dummy velocity inflated by a position jump between steps, or a car velocity that includes lateral or truncation effects. The Builder did not run the checks.

The lock never releases once set, so a car that swerved stays offset for the rest of its life. This feeds the head-on case above and does not match spec car_to_car rule 10, which says the lock is released when the dummy leaves detection.

repair_requests.problem: Head-on deadlock on level 2, and by the same logic on any level with oncoming traffic. A swerve target that enters an oncoming lane band is allowed and the lock persists.
repair_requests.required_change: 1) In latFree, on levels 1 and 2, reject any target lateral band that overlaps the band of ANY oncoming car in the hall, not only the case where the move reduces lateral distance. Where practical, also reject a target that puts the car in the oncoming lane when an oncoming car could arrive during the swerve. 2) Release c.lock and let the car return to its lane base when the dummy is no longer in conflict (spec rule 10 says the lock is released when the dummy leaves detection). Use the existing 0.96 decay branch to bring c.lat back to 0. 3) Add a head-on resolution so two opposing cars can never both hold at speed 0: for example, in axisMove truncation or the yield logic, a car that is head-on with a stalled opposing car must be handled so the lower-serial car does not wait forever. Re-run levels_always_end_with_dummy_in_traffic, including level 2 seed 7 with the dummy at (245,369).

repair_requests.problem: The damage_follows_momentum check fails: sedan damage 374 where perMomentum x 138 x 1.0 = 228.
repair_requests.required_change: Reproduce the scenario in the check (stationary dummy, sedan cruising at 138). Print c.vx, c.vy, d.vx, d.vy and closing at the moment of impact. Fix whatever inflates closing. Check the dummy velocity after teleports or resets, and the car velocity after truncation or lateral moves. The result must be 228 for a stationary dummy and a 138 sedan, and 1155 at closing 700. Re-run damage_follows_momentum.

repair_requests.problem: The builder reported that no automated checks were run. The two failures show the build was not verified.
repair_requests.required_change: Run the full check suite after the fixes and confirm all 31 pass before resubmitting.

notes: The Builder says learned margins up to 190 px make cars brake more often (they cannot fit within the barriers). This is consistent with the spec, but it may feel harsh in play. It is a tuning matter and not a defect.
Inverse versus direct proportionality in CR-001 is still to be confirmed by Lawrence.
Several perf-sensitive loops are O(n^2) in carsStep. This is acceptable at 12 cars or fewer.
